entries.title: Rear main seal leak; upper seal half siliconed in
entries.text: The rear main seal leaked. A previous owner had siliconed the upper seal half into the block. The lower half came out of the cap but the upper half would not move, so the crank has to come out. (Date approximate: start of the chat.)

entries.title: Chip broke off the rear of the block
entries.text: While punching out the old seal, a chip broke off the very rear of the block, transmission side. Believed non-structural; whether it reaches the seal groove has not been checked. (Date approximate; from the earlier chat.)

entries.title: Crank turned a couple of times with the chain off
entries.text: The crank was turned a couple of times after the chain was off. It turned smoothly with no hard stop, so valve contact is very unlikely. Confirm with a compression or leak-down test after reassembly. Don't turn the crank again until it's out; when it goes back in, set the keyway to match the dot-to-dot photo before the chain goes on.

entries.title: A couple of small nicks on the crank journals
entries.text: Journal cleanup started: knock down raised burrs with oiled 400-600 grit, finish with crocus cloth. Measurements wait on the micrometer. (Date approximate; the Nov 2 work suggests the crank is out.)

entries.title: Status: torn down on the stand, waiting on parts
entries.text: Summit cart held the micrometer (SUM-900014, $64.99), assembly lube and four gaskets (fuel pump, oil pump, water pump, timing cover); ZDDP additive recommended. The rear main seal and oil pan gasket were not in the cart. Next: micrometer arrives, measure journals, order bearings, water pump and timing cover.

entries.title: Old high-school accessory wiring removed
entries.text: The add-on accessory wiring from high school has been removed. Exact date not recorded.

entries.title: Test setup with the engine out
entries.text: With the engine out the body has no factory ground (normally battery negative -> engine -> ground cable at the starter-relay mounting bolt -> body). A temporary jumper now runs from battery negative to that cable at the relay bolt; grounding battery negative to another body point did not work (poor contact). The ground cable's engine end is loose. The starter cable is kept off the relay or insulated. Ignition switch and headlight switch are out of the dash; both front parking/turn connectors are unplugged at the wheel wells. Dates approximate (testing ran Nov 11-12).

entries.title: Starter relay terminal behavior verified
entries.text: Fender-mounted relay, left to right: battery stud, S, I, starter stud; it grounds through its mounting bolt. Battery stud (black/yellow, circuit 37) is hot always. S (red/blue) is hot only in START. I (brown, joined to the pink resistance wire at the firewall main disconnect) is 12 V in ON (through the coil feed) and in START. Starter stud is hot only while cranking.

entries.title: Loose solid-red wire at the relay reads 0 V everywhere
entries.text: A solid-red wire comes from the same firewall main disconnect as the S, I and battery-stud wires. Its relay end is loose and it reads 0 V in every key position. Not identified; trace it with the wiring diagram before connecting it anywhere.

measurements.location: Starter relay end, every key position

entries.title: Ignition switch positions and accessory eyelet
entries.text: Bezel positions are ACC - OFF - ON - START (spring-loaded). An unmarked cylinder-release position counter-clockwise past ACC was mistaken for ACC and caused confusing readings; ignore it. The plug fits one way; a separate eyelet terminal on the back is the accessory feed, circuit 297 (black-green), which feeds the turn-signal flasher (circuit 8). Verified with correct positions: S hot only in START; pink coil feed and brown hot in ON and START.

entries.title: Pink resistance wire: 12 V unloaded, lower under coil load
entries.text: The pink resistance wire reads a full 12 V unloaded. Under coil load it drops to roughly 6-9 V. Never use it as a switched-power source for accessories.

measurements.what: Pink resistance wire, under coil load
measurements.location: Coil feed; roughly 6-9 V (approximate, no single reading recorded)

entries.title: Headlight switch crackles and breaker cycles in the parking position
entries.text: In the parking (middle) position the headlight switch crackled and its breaker made a ding; the taillights blinked as the breaker reset, and the front parking lights never lit.

entries.title: Short on circuit 11 isolated to the passenger front parking wiring
entries.text: The short to ground is on circuit 11 (front parking lights), in the passenger-side wiring past the wheel-well connector. Unplugging that connector stopped the crackling; unplugging the driver side did not. Next: battery off, bulb out, ohm wire 11 to ground to find the spot.

entries.title: Crackle at the starter relay was arcing at the ground bolt
entries.text: The crackle heard at the starter relay was arcing at the relay-bolt ground connection, with short-circuit current returning through it. It was not the relay switching. Clean and tighten that ground.

entries.title: Headlight switch continuity map: switch looks fine
entries.text: From the owner's chart (see photo). Battery (B) connects to A in Off (plus I-R through the dash-light dimmer); to R, P, I, A in the middle (park) position; to R, H, I, A fully out (headlights). P is front parking (live only in the middle position; they go off when the headlights come on), R is taillights, H headlights, I instrument lights, D1/D2 likely dome/courtesy, A unconfirmed. The switch appears to work as designed.

entries.title: Dash-light feed is a blue wire, not a ground
entries.text: The blue dash-light wire with a three-way splitter reads grounded with the lights off (through the dash bulbs) and is powered, dimmed by the headlight knob, with the lights on. It is not a ground. It has a spare unused branch, a good source for the tach light and radio illumination.

entries.title: Brake lights work: rear wiring, sockets and bulbs are good
entries.text:
Proves the rear wiring, sockets and bulbs, and the turn-signal switch's brake contacts.

*Corrected 2026-11-14:* still correct. These are the lever switch's brake contacts.

entries.title: Hazard flasher confirmed good, and its always-hot feed
entries.text:
A jumper test made a rear light blink through the flasher, and its orange feed jumpered to a rear pin gave a steady light.

*Corrected 2026-11-14:* this was the **hazard flasher**, not the turn-signal flasher. Its orange feed is always hot (battery through a fuse), not circuit 8.

entries.title: Hazard flasher blue good to the four-wire block; fronts read 0 V
entries.text:
A jumper from the blue terminal at the four-wire block to a rear pin blinked. With everything connected, that blue read 12 V but white-blue and green-white read 0 V in every lever position.

*Corrected 2026-11-14:* the four-wire block is the **terminal board of the missing hazard switch**, and its blue is the hazard flasher's output. The turn-signal flasher has its own blue (44) going to the lever switch's plug at the column base. The fronts read 0 V because the hazard switch is missing and the turn-signal flasher is dead.

entries.title: Flasher terminals read 12 V with the key OFF (explained: hazard flasher)
entries.text:
Both flasher terminals read 12 V even with the key off.

*Corrected 2026-11-14:* that is the **hazard flasher**, which is meant to be always hot so hazards work with the key off. Nothing wrong.

entries.title: Heater fan: motor, power and resistor work; factory switch never grounds
entries.text: The '66 blower is switched on the ground side (forum source): the motor has power on one wire and the switch grounds it through the resistor taps (high = no resistor). Grounding a resistor terminal with a jumper runs the fan, so motor, power and resistor are good. The factory switch, with its housing grounded, never grounds any output in any position. Decision: replace the heater fan switch.

entries.title: Uncle's potentiometer wiring removed from the heater fan
entries.text: The motor's control wire is now on the resistor.

entries.title: Testing lessons
entries.text: Continuity tests mislead wherever bulbs or motors are connected (cold filaments read near 0 ohm), so pull bulbs or unplug loads first. Use a current-limited test light, not a bare jumper, when hunting shorts. Battery disconnected: multimeter ohms/continuity. Battery connected: voltage or test light. Back-probing means sliding a thin probe in from behind beside the wire at a plugged-in connector.

entries.title: Ordered the micrometer set, assembly lube, and all gaskets and seals
entries.text: Includes the rear main seal, oil pan gasket set, front crank seal, and the fuel pump, oil pump, pickup, water pump, timing cover, thermostat and valve cover gaskets. Still to order: water pump, new timing cover, and bearings once the journals are measured.

entries.title: Crank out
entries.text: Rod caps off, rubber hose over the rod bolts, pistons pushed up out of the way, and the crank wiggled out.

entries.title: Broken-off block piece JB Welded back on
entries.text: Looks good. It still needs sanding flush.

entries.text: Painless CirKit Boss 70107 kit, wire, connectors and terminals, fuses, grommets, sleeve and harness tape.

entries.title: Unused switched 12 V wire and a three-prong illumination plug under the dash
entries.text: An unused switched 12 V wire under the dash, probably the factory radio feed. Also a three-prong plug that seemed to be for illuminating something. Wire color, key positions and location are not recorded yet.

entries.title: Rod caps, main caps and bearing shells laid out in order and marked
Pick the stuck upper seal half out of the block groove
Rear shocks and spring shackles on hand
entries.text: New rear shocks and leaf-spring shackles are bought and waiting. The front shocks were already replaced earlier; the rears were put off for the engine and wiring work.

entries.title: New tires on hand, not mounted yet
entries.text: New tires are bought but not mounted, since the car can't be driven to a shop. Plan: pull the wheels and take them in.

entries.title: When the blinkers stopped
entries.text: The turn signals worked on both sides around Nov 11. They stopped after the old accessory wiring came out and before the parking-light crackle, so the circuit-11 short didn't cause it.

entries.title: Lever switch continuity: passes
entries.text: Battery off, the lever switch's six-wire plug (four turn-signal wires plus two horn) and two-wire plug unplugged, switch side only. Blue switches to the correct front and rear with the lever; nothing in neutral; green-red (brake) reaches both rears in neutral. The brake-while-signaling check (step 4) wasn't completed.

entries.title: Orange flasher feed is spliced into the cigarette lighter's feed
entries.text: Following the orange wire from the flasher: instead of going to the ignition switch accessory eyelet (black-green), it is spliced into a blue wire feeding the factory cigarette lighter. Per the 2026-11-14 findings, this was the **hazard flasher's** always-hot feed, so the splice is likely how the hazard flasher gets constant power. Whether it is factory or added later isn't known.

entries.title: The four-wire block is the hazard switch's terminal board (switch missing)
entries.text: The four-wire block the earlier tests centered on is the back/terminal board of the 1965–66 emergency-flasher (hazard) switch. The toggle switch is missing, so the block has no mating half. Terminals: blue = hazard flasher output (in); green-white, white-blue and green-red are spliced into the lever switch's left front, right front and brake wires. The 1966 REV1 exterior-lights diagram shows a separate EM flasher (fuse #5, 20 A, from battery) and a hazard warning switch.

entries.title: Jumper tests at the hazard board prove the lever switch and rears
entries.text: Blue jumped to one other terminal at a time. The power back-feeds through the lever switch, which proves its selector contacts, the rear wiring and the rear bulbs. Unverified: the diagram predicts the green-red jumper with the lever in a turn position lights only one rear; both were seen.

entries.title: Jumping hazard blue to the front wire is not a fix
entries.text: With the driver front light reconnected, blue jumped to green-white made the driver front blink constantly in every lever position, confirming green-white runs straight to the front light. A permanent jumper would make the fronts and dash arrows blink all the time, even key-off, and drain the battery. The driver front also blinked with the green-red jumper; if the lever was in neutral, that suggests a miswire at that light.

entries.title: Factory turn-signal flasher reads open: dead
entries.text: Found the factory turn-signal flasher (separate from the hazard flasher). Old thermal flashers are closed when cold and should read continuous. It reads open across its terminals; the hazard flasher reads continuous. Next: swap test, then replace.

entries.title: Blew the primary switched 12 V fuse while testing at the driver front light
entries.text: Swapping wires at the driver front light while live shorted the circuit. Afterward neither the hazard flasher's blue nor its orange feed had power. The blown fuse has been found. Sort out the driver front wires before replacing it. Owner: this is the car's primary switched 12 V fuse, not a hazard-only fuse.

entries.title: Got the 1966 wiring diagrams
entries.text: The factory 1966 'Exterior Lighting, Turn Signals and Horns' diagram (averagejoerestoration.com, 66exter1.jpg) and the 1966 REV1 6/10/22 exterior-lights diagram, page 3 of 5 (vintage-mustang.com), which has a 'How the turn switch operates' panel. Shared as images in another chat; not yet saved here.

entries.title: Decided to remove the hazard system instead of restoring it
entries.text: Hazards aren't wanted. The plan is to remove the hazard board and its wires, the always-hot orange feed at the lighter splice, and the hazard flasher, after the turn-signal flasher swap test (which uses the hazard flasher as the known-good unit). The hazard switch is no longer needed.

entries.title: Hazard harness removed
entries.text: The entire hazard (emergency flasher) harness is out of the car and on the bench, including the four-terminal board and the hazard flasher. The orange feed was pulled off the constant-12 V wire in the dash (the cigarette lighter's feed), which is taped off for now. Not recorded: whether the board's wires were plugged in or spliced into the lever switch wires.

entries.title: Replace the blown hazard-circuit fuse (only after the driver front wires are sorted), then confirm the hazard flasher's orange feed has power
Key on: test light on each terminal of the turn-signal flasher's socket; one should light (orange-yellow 8)
Swap test: plug the good hazard flasher into the turn-signal flasher's socket, all four bulbs connected; pull the lever left and right
